benefits.name: Montana Disabled Veteran (MDV) Property Tax Assistance Program
benefits.description: Montana reduces the property tax rate on a primary residence for veterans with a 100% service-connected disability (or their unmarried surviving spouse), on a sliding scale of 50% to 100% reduction based on income and filing status. For tax year 2026, single filers with federal adjusted gross income under $62,598 qualify (100% reduction up to $48,152, phasing down to 50% at $57,782-$62,598); married/head-of-household filers qualify under $72,229 (100% reduction up to $57,781, phasing down to 50% at $67,413-$72,229); unmarried surviving spouses qualify under $54,573 (100% reduction up to $40,127, phasing down to 50% at $49,759-$54,573). The homeowner must own or be under contract to purchase the home and occupy it as a primary residence at least 7 months per year. Applications are due April 15 (late applications considered for the following year).
benefits.value: Property tax rate reduced 50%-100% depending on income tier and filing status

otherReqs: 100% disability rating from a service-connected injury per VA letter
Own or be under contract to purchase the home; occupy as primary residence at least 7 months per year
Income limits apply (2026: single <$62,598; married/HOH <$72,229; unmarried surviving spouse <$54,573)
Application due April 15

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate Fee Waiver
benefits.description: Montana waives the veterans' cemetery fee and all motor vehicle registration fees for two non-commercial vehicles for veterans who are Purple Heart recipients with a 50% or more service-connected disability rating (cemetery fee not waived for this category), or who have a 100% VA disability rating (or are paid at the 100% disabled rate for a service-connected disability). The Disabled Veteran plate also authorizes disabled parking privileges. A letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs stating the disability rating or payment status is required, and applicants apply through their local county treasurer.
benefits.value: Registration fee and veterans' cemetery fee waived for two non-commercial vehicles

otherReqs: Purple Heart recipients need 50%+ service-connected disability rating (cemetery fee not waived for this tier)
100% VA disability rating (or 100% disabled pay rate) qualifies for full waiver including cemetery fee
Vehicles must be non-commercial
Apply through local county treasurer

application.agency: Montana Motor Vehicle Division / County Treasurer
documentation: Letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs stating disability rating or payment status

benefits.name: Combat-Disabled Veteran Half-Price Deer/Antelope License
benefits.description: Montana veterans with certain combat-connected injuries may qualify for half-priced deer and antelope hunting licenses. Up to 50 such licenses are issued annually. Applicants must submit the annual Combat Disabled Application and contact Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks Licensing to confirm which combat-connected injuries qualify.
benefits.value: 50% discount on deer and antelope hunting licenses (limited to 50 licenses annually)

otherReqs: Must have a qualifying combat-connected injury (specific criteria confirmed by FWP Licensing)
Limited to 50 licenses issued per year
Combat Disabled Application form required

benefits.name: VA Hospital Patient Free Fishing / Purple Heart Conservation License
benefits.description: Veterans who are current patients at a VA hospital may fish in Montana without a license, provided they carry documentation signed by VA hospital staff confirming their patient status. Separately, residents and nonresidents who have been awarded a Purple Heart, regardless of age, may fish and hunt upland game birds with a Conservation License issued by Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks upon verification of the Purple Heart award and DD-214.
benefits.value: Free fishing for VA hospital patients; free upland-bird hunting/fishing Conservation License for Purple Heart recipients

otherReqs: VA hospital patients must carry documentation signed by VA hospital staff confirming current patient status
Purple Heart recipients must provide Purple Heart verification and DD-214

documentation: VA hospital patient documentation, or Purple Heart award verification and DD-214

benefits.name: Honorably Discharged Veteran Tuition Waiver
benefits.description: The Montana University System waives remaining in-state tuition (as a last-dollar award, after all other financial aid is applied) for honorably discharged veterans who are Montana residents attending a qualifying MUS campus. The veteran must have received an Honorable discharge (Honorable Under General Conditions is not accepted) for active duty service other than for training purposes, must have elected to become eligible for VA education benefits under Title 38 or Title 10 but had those benefits expire or become exhausted, must apply no later than the third week of the first semester, and must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress. The waiver does not cover flat fees and applies to both undergraduate and graduate students.
benefits.value: Last-dollar waiver of remaining in-state tuition after other aid is applied

otherReqs: Honorable discharge for active duty service other than training
VA Title 38/Title 10 education benefits must be expired or exhausted
Apply no later than the third week of the first semester
Must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress per campus SAP policy

documentation: Proof VA education benefits are expired/exhausted

benefits.name: Veterans' Employment Preference (State Hiring)
benefits.description: Under MCA 39-29-102, when a Montana public employer uses a scored hiring procedure, an applicant must have added to their score 5 percentage points if a veteran, or 10 percentage points if a disabled veteran or eligible relative (a disabled veteran cannot stack both). The applicant must still meet the position's minimum qualifications to receive the points. When a public employer uses a non-scored selection procedure, preference is given, in order, to disabled veterans, persons with disabilities, veterans, eligible relatives, and eligible spouses over any nonpreferred applicant with substantially equal qualifications.
benefits.value: 5 percentage-point score preference for veterans; 10 percentage-point preference for disabled veterans/eligible relatives

otherReqs: Applicant must meet the position's minimum qualifications to receive preference points
Disabled veteran preference (10 points) and veteran preference (5 points) cannot be combined

documentation: DD-214 or proof of veteran/disabled veteran status

benefits.name: Montana State Veterans Homes
benefits.description: Montana operates three state veterans nursing homes — in Columbia Falls (Montana Veterans' Home, 105 intermediate/skilled-care beds plus 12 domiciliary beds, including a 15-bed Alzheimer's unit), Butte, and Glendive. The Columbia Falls home is Medicare/Medicaid and VA certified and is directed by the Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services, an executive agency of state government. The Columbia Falls facility has served veterans since 1896.
benefits.value: Skilled nursing and domiciliary care at three state-operated veterans homes

otherReqs: Medicare/Medicaid and VA certification requirements apply
Specific admission criteria set by DPHHS, not detailed on the summary page fetched this session

application.agency: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service
